situation: My newest hire is better at part of the job than I am and we both know it.

dims.SPEAKABILITY: Card 2's lines are more natural and confident ("You are ahead of me on this particular skill and I am not going to pretend otherwise"), while Card 1's opening ("actually a good problem to have") and "build around it, not around it" phrasing sound more managed and slightly stilted.
dims.SPECIFICITY: Both invoke the same dynamic, but Card 2's "I have made most of the expensive mistakes already" concretely names what the manager offers in trade, whereas Card 1 stays at the level of generic "high standard" language.
dims.TIGHTNESS: Card 1's commitment section repeats "the same bar" / "high standard" ideas twice and pads with reassurance, while Card 2's script lands each beat once and moves on.
dims.HONESTY: Both hold the standard, but Card 2 more crisply names the uncomfortable trade — the manager admitting the gap out loud AND asserting real value in return — without softening into warmth as Card 1's LONG GAME does.

PICK: 2

SPEAKABILITY: Card 2's lines are more natural and confident ("You are ahead of me on this particular skill and I am not going to pretend otherwise"), while Card 1's opening ("actually a good problem to have") and "build around it, not around it" phrasing sound more managed and slightly stilted.

SPECIFICITY: Both invoke the same dynamic, but Card 2's "I have made most of the expensive mistakes already" concretely names what the manager offers in trade, whereas Card 1 stays at the level of generic "high standard" language.

TIGHTNESS: Card 1's commitment section repeats "the same bar" / "high standard" ideas twice and pads with reassurance, while Card 2's script lands each beat once and moves on.

HONESTY: Both hold the standard, but Card 2 more crisply names the uncomfortable trade — the manager admitting the gap out loud AND asserting real value in return — without softening into warmth as Card 1's LONG GAME does.
